newsitem.title: UK: Tide turning for aluminium - J.P.Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Tide turning for aluminium - J.P.Morgan.

text.p: The tide is turning for aluminium prices after a bleak year so far in 1996, according to Kevin Crisp of U.S. investment house J.P.Morgan.
Addressing a London Metal Exchange (LME) seminar he forecast average aluminumium prices to rise to $1,680 per tonne in 1997 from $1,524 in 1996.
"We think the tide for aluminium is already turning," Crisp said.
The fall in prices during the last few weeks was merely "fog on the road," he said.
Aluminium consumption is set to grow by 4.4 percent next year from 0.8 percent this year but the rate of growth of output is set to fall to 5.4 percent in 1997 from seven in 1996.
Imports to the Western world from other countries are set to fall.

Crisp forecast imports of 1.87 million tonnes in 1997 from 2.14 million in 1996. He said Russian exports to the West were set to drop several hundred thousand tonnes next year as domestic consumption grew.
Crisp said that while LME stcoks have risen in 1996 producer stocks had fallen, leaving reported stocks around level.
But unreported stocks have risen, he added.
"Total unreported stocks of metal tied up in financing deals could be in the order of 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes," Crisp said.
He said prices would rise more sharply in 1998, but sustained high prices led to the threat of substiution.
"The lack of new capacity could lead to surging prices over the few years....and could lead to significant substitution," he said.
